title: Classifier output enforced by a provider JSON schema, not prompt prose plus an exact parser
description: Raw captures on 2026-09-04 showed the slot classifier's free-JSON output drifts with every prompt change (an option written into the outcome field cost 11 of 265 slot entries; one completion in 36 was cut mid-string). title: Content coverage: every deliverable the user enumerated reaches the plan's output contract
description: Evidence (172-case 3a leg, 84 missed expected field groups): 15 groups were cited by the classifier as named results but dropped by the planner; 25 were never cited (enumerations in prose the classifier did not read as the result's contents); 22 were cited as clauses (A0-Q2 fixes the naming). Design: (1) admission: a proposal whose steps carry no leaf for a cited named result is repaired or refused at the result contract (ai_builder_result_contract / proposal admission), so the planner cannot drop a cited deliverable; (2) reader recall: the classifier prompt's named_result rule reads 'flödet ska ta fram X, Y och Z' as the result's contents when the terminal output is structured or a report; (3) the 'no JSON step' cases (a text reply built without a structured analysis step) are architecture, measured separately. Measure on the leaf-fields cohort x3 + broad x1. Slice E (m55.24) is not needed: the citation mechanism exists.

comments.text: Root cause found 2026-09-04: named_result_projection (ai_builder_action_policy.py) returns None unless terminal_output is structured_json, so for report, text and DOCX/PDF flows the cited deliverables are only a prompt rule ('include every final-report fact in the source-reading JSON output_fields') with no admission check; the 'cited but plan missing' losses are almost all report flows. Extension: (1) named_result_projection also projects for report terminals; (2) the predicate verifies against the verification step = the terminal when it declares output_fields, else the last structured step before the terminal (the source-reading JSON step the writer consumes); (3) the prompt rule names that step instead of 'the FINAL step'; (4) the compiler postcondition uses the same step choice. title: Builder asks whether the transcript should label speakers (vemsa diarization)
description:
Owner request 2026-09-03 (after wiring vemsa to the :8144 lane): when a brief needs a transcription step and the tenant's transcription service is configured for diarization, the Builder should ask whether the transcript should mark who says what, and build the whole speaker experience when the answer is yes.

Design (fits commit 3a's interaction policy table):
- Slot 'speaker_identification' in ai_builder_slot_interaction_policy.py, values label_speakers | plain_transcript. Relevant only when primary_runtime_input is audio AND the transcription service is configured with mode diarize (settings flag flow_transcription_service_configured + mode passed into the discovery context; not relevant otherwise, so tenants without vemsa never see it). when_unknown = ask. has_explicit_text = wording about speakers/participants (vem som säger vad, talare, deltagare) makes it an ask, never a silent default. No preselection (owner UI decision).
- Question catalog entry (Swedish): 'Ska transkriptet märka upp vem som säger vad?' with options 'Ja, märk upp talarna' / 'Nej, löpande text'; one-line helper that names are mapped from a participants field.
- Materialization (flow_draft_materialization.py already writes wizard.transcription_enabled + transcription_model from default_transcription_model_id): also write wizard.transcription_diarization from the slot. When label_speakers: add a participants list form field ('Vilka deltog?') and a speaker_mapping step after the transcription step, mirroring the editor template in FlowEditor.ts (participantsField, buildSpeakerMappingOutputConfig, review_policy edit); later prompt steps reference the named speakers.
- Frontend: the Builder question card renders the two options with the existing shadcn option control; the created flow opens with Talaridentifiering on in stage 2.
- Tests: relevance off without the service; asked with audio + service; explicit speaker wording asks; every assume writes plain_transcript; materialization writes metadata + participants field + speaker_mapping step; runtime parity with the editor-built flow.

Lands after A0 commit 3a (Beads m55.21) because the policy table is the owner.

title: Evidence-driven flow review: analyze a flow's runs in the Builder edit session and propose verified improvements
description: Owner decision 2026-09-04: keep it small. One deterministic, bounded, classification-redacted evidence packet per flow built from what runs already persist (definition, step inputs and outputs, provenance edges, metrics, warnings, errors), viewable and downloadable by the user. One review task, one model call, typed ranked findings each quoting evidence and proposing an edit (unused step output, duplicated steps, instruction versus outcome drift, cost concentration). Discussion and application go through the existing edit session, admission, projection and critic. Fixed invariant: the review model's security classification is at least the flow's, chosen from the space's Builder models, typed refusal otherwise, never a downgrade. title: Make semantic proposal repair converge without terminal errors
description:
TL;DR: A valid Flow architecture can still terminate during proposal self-correction when a compositional text step fails to consume all relevant structured predecessors. Preserve the critic and make the canonical typed repair path converge generally, without case-, prompt-, filename-, or corpus-keyed behavior.

Problem and evidence

Report-layout R4 candidate C1 produced `self_correction_quality_failure` with typed code `final_text_step_must_reference_relevant_structured_outputs` on an otherwise valid document-to-DOCX-template architecture. Exact parent completed the same control first pass. The same exact candidate completed it first pass in R3, so the failure is provider-plan variance reaching a real fail-closed repair seam, not evidence of a deterministic report-layout transformation defect. R4 stopped before repeats and all 172-case legs. Immutable receipt and verdict identities are recorded on measurement task `eneo-flow-ai-builder-production-readiness-m55.5`.

Why it matters

The user sees a terminal Builder error after answering a valid canonical question. A retry may succeed, but relying on provider luck violates the production no-hard-failure gate. Weakening the critic would allow under-bound plans and is not acceptable.

Current and proposed canonical ownership

The typed invariant remains owned by `ai_builder_critic_invariants.py`. Failure classification remains owned by proposal finalization. Repair convergence should remain in the existing proposal self-correction/retry owner; do not add a second repair service, a case-specific compiler branch, or another prompt-only fallback. First determine whether the correct smallest complete solution is better typed repair feedback, a deterministic owner-level normalization already supported by the plan contract, or deletion/consolidation of a duplicate repair path.

Scope and non-goals

- Reproduce the generic topology class from typed plan contracts, not from the benchmark wording or fixture.
- Inventory preserved receipt incidence for this exact failure code across parent/candidate history and distinguish deterministic source behavior from provider variance.
- Add behavior-first RED proof at the stable proposal finalization/retry boundary.
- Implement only a general canonical-owner correction that preserves compiler, critic, source-evidence, architecture, and no-retry contracts.
- Do not change report-layout questions, corpus, fixtures, expectations, benchmark adjudication, provider model, broad classifier authority, or failure floors.
- Do not weaken or special-case `final_text_step_must_reference_relevant_structured_outputs`.

Acceptance criteria

1. A generic valid architecture with at least two relevant structured producers cannot terminate solely because the repaired compositional step omits one producer; the existing typed repair owner either produces a critic-valid plan within the bounded retry contract or returns an explicit non-retryable cause that is not falsely presented as provider success.
2. Existing invalid plans are still rejected by the critic.
3. DOCX template-fill, generated document, report-layout, form-field, and unrelated simple-flow behavior remain unchanged.
4. No case-, corpus-, prompt-, localized phrase-, file-, or model-ID keyed production logic.
5. Decisive isolated tests, full Builder unit suite, full Flow unit suite, relevant integrations, canonical Pyright, Ruff/format, hooks, and one exact-diff Codex peer gate score at least 8 pass before commit.
6. Any provider-backed remeasurement uses a new integrated candidate, prospective addendum, fresh roots/spaces, ten-minute minimum plus exact-parent health gate, all targeted repetitions, then all six fresh 172-case legs. No landing on any hard, quality, repair, expectation, question, latency, call, or token breach.

Recovery

Keep the report-layout candidate `985aa3f3b3009d22144ad691643101548166fa78` unpushed. If the general repair cannot be proved without broadening ownership or weakening a contract, make no source change and return for an explicit owner decision.
acceptance_criteria: Typed generic repair convergence is proven without weakening critic or adding case-specific logic; deterministic suites and peer gate pass; provider-backed no-regression measurement remains required before landing.

title: Keep report topology channels aligned after lowering
description:
TL;DR: A valid multi-source report can terminate before proposal creation when document-report lowering changes a step's predecessor from TEXT to JSON but retains the previously derived input channel. Recompute the server-owned derived channel from final lowered adjacency so all supported report layouts compile without weakening typed validation.

## Problem and impact

R2 produced a hard `architecture_materialization_failed` for an explicit report whose classifier evidence and architecture commit were correct. The report lowerer replaced a weak TEXT section writer with a structured JSON section writer. A following retained JSON overview step still carried `underlag_channel=implicit_previous`, derived against the removed TEXT predecessor; the final JSON-to-TEXT boundary requires `whole_object`. This is a latent general compiler bug exposed by the new architecture gate, not a benchmark-specific miss.

## Ownership

- Current and proposed canonical owner: `ai_builder_assembly/document_report/lowering.py`, which owns the structural rewrite.
- Invariant owner to preserve: `ai_builder_assembly/plan.py::derive_underlag_channel` plus `FlowAssemblyPlan` validation.
- Reuse the existing derivation function after final report adjacency is known. Do not duplicate its rules, weaken validation, or create a generic repair service.

## Smallest complete slice

- Add a provider-neutral compiler behavior test for a reader JSON → weak section TEXT → retained overview JSON → terminal TEXT outline.
- Prove all non-null report dispositions remain valid after lowering, while the exact `both` shape produces the deterministic compose topology.
- Re-derive the server-owned underlag channel for lowered previous-step adjacency at the report-lowering boundary.

## Deliberate non-goals

- No classifier, prompt, question, architecture-gate, provider adapter, harness, corpus, fixture, expectation, runtime execution, UI, migration, or public API change.
- No case ID, phrase, filename, language token, model-output name, or report-specific exception in the typed validator.
- Do not cherry-pick unrelated historical aggregate-contract or extraction-warning candidates.

## Validation

- RED/GREEN focused compiler regression.
- Existing report-disposition compiler matrix and assembly-plan invariants.
- Full Flow AI Builder unit suite, full Flow unit suite, relevant integration tests, canonical Pyright, Ruff, format, diff check, and repository hooks.
- One exact-staged Codex xhigh peer gate before local commit. No push.

## Risk and rollback

Risk is bounded to server-owned report topology projection. Incorrect broad normalization could mask provider defects, so only the derived channel may change and the typed plan validator remains authoritative. Rollback is the single local commit; R2 receipts remain immutable and cannot be rerun under the same addendum.
acceptance_criteria: A provider-neutral report outline whose lowering replaces a weak TEXT section producer with JSON compiles successfully for every non-null report layout; final previous-step channels equal derive_underlag_channel for their actual predecessor; existing fail-closed plan validation and unrelated Builder behavior remain unchanged; all declared deterministic gates pass; local commit only, no push.
